title: Reverse string
md:
## The idea

Swap the first and last characters, then the second and second-last, moving both pointers inward until they meet.

## Step by step

1. i = 0, j = last.
2. While i < j: swap s[i] and s[j]; i++, j--.

## Worked example

**Input:** s = "hello"

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| swap h, o | "oellh" |
| swap e, l | "olleh" |
| i meets j | stop |

**Result:** "olleh"

## Cost

O(n) time, O(1) memory.

## The code (C#, compiled and tested against every part of the question)

```csharp
// LeetCode 344 — reverse a character array in place, O(1) extra memory.
public static class ReverseString {
    public static void InPlace(char[] s) {
        if (s == null) return;
        int i = 0, j = s.Length - 1;
        while (i < j) {                        // swap the two ends and move inwards
            char t = s[i]; s[i] = s[j]; s[j] = t;
            i++; j--;
        }
    }
}
```

## Likely follow-up questions

**Q: Emoji and other surrogate pairs?**

Reversing UTF-16 code units splits them. Reverse text elements (StringInfo) if real text matters.

**Q: Complexity?**

O(n) time, O(1) memory.

**Q: Shared state?**

It mutates the caller's array.

**Q: Reverse the words of a sentence in place.**

Reverse the whole array, then reverse each word — LeetCode 186/151.

**Q: Why is this on a Staff list?**

It usually opens into the word-reversal or Unicode follow-up — be ready to go there.
